note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 (independent auditor) after the user-namespace conversion (25fbb6e890/d8427e4380): the TestVRRPOwnerAnswersWithVirtualMACOnly and TestVRRPNonOwnerMasterAnswersARPWithVirtualMACOnly unit gained only `if !userns.Enter(t) { return }` as its first statement and its build tag moved from integration&&linux to linux. userns.Enter (internal/test/userns/userns_linux.go) re-runs the one named test in a fresh user+net+mount namespace and returns false to the parent only when the child reported PASS or SKIP; a failing child, a non-zero exit, or a child that ran nothing calls t.Fatalf, so every assertion below the guard still fails the test when the behaviour breaks. Body otherwise byte-identical. RFC 3768 Section 8.2: "When a host sends an ARP request for one of the virtual router IP addresses, the Master virtual router MUST respond to the ARP request with the virtual MAC address for the virtual router." Fresh judgement: both units require an ARP reply carrying the virtual MAC (owner via the owner filter, non-owner via the recipe), contrasted with the physical-MAC control and, for the non-owner, no reply once the address is removed. Enforced.
